strengths: Addresses a clear and important gap in existing benchmarks—mathematical reasoning with image-based answer options is underrepresented despite being common in educational practice
High-quality dataset construction with careful curation from authentic exam papers, multiple expert annotators, balanced answer distributions, and comprehensive quality control
Comprehensive evaluation of 36 diverse LMMs across multiple model families and scales with well-designed experiments including ablations and multiple analytical angles
Valuable empirical findings including quantified performance degradation with image similarity, identification of positional bias, and insights about deep thinking model performance
Strong experimental design with unified prompts, consistent evaluation settings, and ablation studies examining effects of image merging and text labels
Clear presentation with effective use of examples, tables, and figures to communicate findings
weaknesses: Limited novelty—this is fundamentally a dataset/benchmark paper without methodological innovation or proposed solutions to the identified problems
Significant accessibility limitation due to Chinese-language-only dataset; reduces impact for international research community and reproducibility concerns

Evaluation methodology gaps including lack of human baseline for difficulty calibration, unreported inter-annotator agreement statistics, and potential noise from using GLM4-Flash for answer extraction

Insufficient depth of analysis—missing qualitative error examples, topic-level difficulty breakdown, investigation of why deep thinking models underperform, and validation of similarity metric against actual LMM perception

Unclear distinction from prior work: MV-Math already includes 595 image-based option questions; positioning as 'first' dataset could be more nuanced regarding the incremental nature of this contribution
Positional bias identified but not deeply investigated; no mitigation strategies proposed or analysis of consistency across model families and sizes
Limited actionable insights for model development; findings presented as observations rather than recommendations for addressing identified challenges
Dataset scale (1,800 questions) is reasonable but not large by modern standards; 48.1% stem-image split deserves deeper analysis
Missing statistical rigor in some analyses; correlation analysis lacks consistent significance testing and effect size reporting

strengths: Novel and well-motivated problem formulation addressing a genuine gap in multimodal mathematical evaluation benchmarks, specifically targeting image-based answer choices that require fine-grained visual discrimination
High-quality, carefully curated dataset from authoritative sources (Chinese entrance exams 2002-2023) with rigorous quality control, expert cross-annotation, and balanced answer distributions
Comprehensive evaluation of 36 diverse LMMs spanning different model families and scales, providing a thorough baseline assessment of current capabilities

Insightful analytical findings including discovery of positional biases toward option A (44.8% in image-stem conditions), clear performance degradation with image similarity (26.4% drop for top models), and systematic comparison of single-image vs. multi-image approaches
Sophisticated analysis methodology with correlation studies across model classes, stratified performance by image similarity, and meaningful ablations examining text-image binding effects
Reproducible and transparent methodology with detailed documentation of data collection, cleaning procedures, and evaluation protocols
weaknesses: Limited to Chinese language and Chinese educational context, significantly restricting generalizability and potential impact for international AI research community; no discussion of cross-lingual transferability

Critical absence of human performance baseline, making it impossible to interpret whether model performance (45.9% best) represents acceptable challenge or systemic failure; no inter-annotator agreement metrics reported

Evaluation methodology ambiguity: abstract mentions 'few-shot exemplars with chain-of-thought prompting' while methods section claims 'zero-shot setting'—this contradiction requires clarification and affects interpretation
Limited error analysis and failure mode investigation; paper identifies performance gaps but lacks qualitative examples of common mistakes or categorization by problem type (geometry, algebra, etc.)
Primarily a benchmark contribution without methodological novelty or proposed solutions; paper is descriptive rather than prescriptive about addressing identified LMM limitations

Incomplete analysis: missing statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, variance estimates, inter-annotator agreement, and limited ablation coverage; tables 3-4 are dense and difficult to parse

Insufficient justification for improvement over related work (e.g., clear distinction from MV-Math's 595 image-option questions not emphasized early); dataset bias and topic distribution not thoroughly analyzed

strengths: Well-motivated benchmark addressing a genuine gap in evaluating LMMs' ability to reason over highly similar visual options, which is common in mathematics education

High-quality dataset construction with 1,800 problems from real entrance exams (2002-2023), careful curation, dual annotation, balanced answer distribution, and systematic quantification of visual similarity
Comprehensive evaluation of 20+ diverse LMMs with proper experimental controls, consistent prompting, deterministic decoding, and model version tracking
Insightful error analysis identifying image-text misalignment as dominant failure mode (36%), validated through controlled shuffling experiments
Three complementary strategies for performance improvement, with Strategy 3 achieving +12.6% gain on limited CoT data, demonstrating value of explicit visual-textual alignment
Strong reproducibility with detailed appendices, complete prompt specifications, CoT dataset construction details, and version documentation
Clear presentation of three key observations: single-image LMMs fail at multi-image reasoning, stem images increase task difficulty, and performance degrades with visual similarity
weaknesses: Limited scope restricted to K-12 mathematics; external validity to other domains (physics, chemistry, engineering) unclear; all problems from Chinese exams, limiting generalizability
Error analysis only on GLM4.5V with 50 samples; no inter-annotator agreement metrics; would benefit from analyzing other models, especially top performers like Gemini 2.5 Pro
Visual similarity metric using Qwen-embedding-v1 not justified; alternative embeddings could yield different distributions; bimodal distribution in Figure 3(c) unexplained

CoT fine-tuning (Strategy 3) only evaluated on single small model (Qwen2.5-VL-3B); uses other models for data generation (QwenVL-Max, DeepSeek V3.1) with potential systematic bias; only 500 examples and limited analysis of gains' source

No human performance baseline to contextualize model results; insufficient analysis of why stem-with-images problems are consistently harder; limited exploration of alternative approaches for single-image models

Benchmark size (1,800) smaller than some contemporaries; no reporting of inter-annotator agreement or annotation quality metrics; many problems appear to have obvious distractors given bimodal similarity distribution
Strategy 2 shows modest gains (+0.9% for Gemini 2.5 Pro); missing mechanistic analysis of why strategies work; Strategy 1's potential input length issues not discussed

Missing ablation studies on design choices; no stratification by difficulty or topic; no analysis of which model families/scales benefit most from strategies; temperature frozen at 0 may not reflect real usage patterns

strengths: Novel benchmark filling genuine gap in multimodal math evaluation focusing on comparative reasoning over highly similar visual options
Rigorous dataset construction from real exam questions (1,800 items) with careful curation, manual review, and balanced answer distributions
Comprehensive evaluation of 20+ LMMs spanning closed-source state-of-the-art and diverse open-source models with multiple evaluation perspectives
Clear identification of image-text misalignment as dominant failure mode (36%) with clever controlled experiments (option shuffling) validating the finding
Demonstration of systematic performance degradation with increasing visual similarity, showing consistent pattern across models
Practical improvement strategies with evidence of effectiveness, including +12.6% gain with limited CoT fine-tuning data
Excellent reproducibility: detailed methodology, experimental settings, version information for closed-source models, and comprehensive prompts in appendices
Well-written paper with clear motivation, good examples, helpful visualizations, and thoughtful discussion of limitations
weaknesses: Limited dataset scope: restricted to K-12 mathematics from Chinese entrance exams; unclear generalization to other domains or non-exam scenarios
Incomplete analysis of improvement strategies: Strategy 3 (CoT fine-tuning) evaluated on only one small model (Qwen2.5-VL-3B), raising questions about generalization to larger model families
Visual similarity metric (Qwen embeddings) lacks justification; no sensitivity analysis or comparison with alternative embedding models
Error analysis limited to 50 cases from single model (GLM-4.5V); insufficient sample size for robust categorization, especially for low-frequency error types (10% knowledge errors)
No human performance baseline, limiting contextualization of model capabilities on the benchmark
Methodological gaps: no inter-annotator agreement statistics reported despite multi-annotator annotation; statistical significance testing absent; no confidence intervals
CoT data generation involves multi-stage pipeline (QwenVL-Max → DeepSeek V3.1) with potential error propagation; filtering for correct answers may introduce dataset bias
Single-image baseline (naive concatenation) is crude; alternative layouts and image presentation strategies untested for fair comparison
